data.summary: Every non-vertical straight line can be written as y = mx + c, where m is the gradient and c is the y-intercept.
key_concepts: Gradient m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1); a vertical line has undefined gradient
c is the value of y when x = 0
Parallel lines share the same gradient

formulas.label: Gradient from two points
formulas.note: Keep the order of subtraction consistent.

formulas.label: Equation of a line
formulas.note: If the line is vertical, write it as x = k.

worked_examples.question: A is (3, -5) and B is (-1, -9). Find the equation of line AB.

common_mistakes.mistake: Computing gradient as change in x over change in y.
common_mistakes.fix: Gradient is change in y over change in x.

common_mistakes.mistake: Mixing the order of points in numerator and denominator.
common_mistakes.fix: If you start with point 2 on top, start with point 2 on the bottom too.

exam_tips: Rearrange given equations into y = mx + c to read the gradient quickly.
Read the axis scales carefully before measuring a gradient off a graph.
